summary: Server callback batch atomicity and the original direct training-step end failure are corrected. Successful math/direct/spawn/ownership contracts remain intact, and ROOT-2C-02 portable historical-writer correction passes independent archive review. One medium lifecycle finding remains: direct train_model persists and exposes accepted controls before a fallible model-update cleanup completes. Reproduced on both interpreters despite 282 passing affected tests each.

findings.title: Direct train_model still accepts canonical controls before fallible model-update cleanup completes.
findings.related_previous_finding: F27-R2-02: the original training-step end-hook failure is fixed; a successful end hook followed by failing model-update cleanup still produces the same rejected-call persistence/retry defect.
findings.cause: After the training-step end hook succeeds, train_model invokes on_train_result_accepted, atomically replaces the canonical ci file and marks successful=True. Its finally then invokes on_train_cleanup(context, True). A public cleanup hook which runs the real cleanup and then raises makes the public call fail after acceptance. There is no rejection handler at this direct boundary. The same failure under train_process is caught by its outer rejection handler while acceptance remains deferred.
findings.test_gap: The delivered cleanup_failure cases always install InterruptEnd, so the end hook has already failed and successful remains False. They verify rejection when a secondary cleanup exception follows an end failure, but omit cleanup failure after otherwise successful training/end hooks.

reproduction.shell: Run each command with zsh -lc. The recorded commands include isolated TMPDIR/cache paths. The reusable reproduce_cleanup_failure.py creates a fresh UUID runtime directory under owned scratch on every invocation; prior results remain retained.
steps: Load the shipped TOML through Config, overriding CPU scalar float64 quadratic model, real SGD momentum=0, lr=.1, epochs=2, two actual samples, N=3, and contained slash model-name paths. Start x=1,c=2,ci=1. Test both an existing canonical ci=1 file and absent canonical state.

Instrument only on_train_cleanup: invoke the actual SCAFFOLD cleanup first, then raise RuntimeError after a real successful training-step end hook. Initialization cleanup is allowed to complete normally. Execute actual train_model and comparison train_process.
Inspect memory ci, canonical bytes/absence, get_update_payload, optimizer pre-hook registration and context flags after the raised exception.

Run actual configure-based 1->2->1 reuse and fresh client-1 reconstruction, then the actual successful client inbound/train/outbound pipeline. Where no canonical file was accepted in the process comparison, explicitly restore the original manually injected ci=1 for the retry; no persistence of unaccepted manual state is assumed.
reproduction.expected: A call rejected by a fallible local end/cleanup hook must retain ci=1 and the exact previous canonical bytes or absence, refuse outbound success, and permit reuse/reconstruction plus explicit ci=1 retry y=.62,ci=.9,delta=-.1.
reproduction.actual_direct: Both canonical-present and canonical-absent train_model calls raise Secondary cleanup failure, but memory ci and canonical ci are .8999999999999995, get_update_payload succeeds, and the file has been replaced/created. Routine reuse and fresh reconstruction adopt .9. Successful retry yields y=.6009999999999999,ci=.895,delta=-.004999999999999449.
reproduction.actual_process_comparison: The same cleanup failure under train_process rejects the pending result, retains memory ci=1 and prior canonical bytes/absence, refuses outbound and retries at .62/.9/-.1.
reproduction.current_failure_result: The independent rejection-asserting regression returns exit 1 on each interpreter: two direct failures and two passing process comparisons. The observational 12-case probe returns zero only after recording observations; its zero exit is not acceptance.

population_consequence.interpretation: Ordinary retry after a caller-visible failure loses the failed attempt delta. This is not a full training-round, external-side-effect or restart rollback requirement.

findings.impact: A failed public direct call becomes durable and outbound-eligible, and routine logical-client reuse changes the next successful local update. The direct/process acceptance inconsistency remains material within the requested lifecycle scope.
findings.bounded_correction: Complete fallible local lifecycle cleanup before direct canonical acceptance, or provide an equivalent bounded rejection boundary preserving the last accepted controls on this error. Keep child controls provisional through model saving/current-token handoff and accept in the parent only after successful loading. Preserve the existing server commit boundary and general accepted fixes. Add this otherwise-successful cleanup failure with canonical-present/absent direct/process comparison and successful reuse/retry. No generic FedAvg redesign or transaction for external side effects is requested.

low_recommendations.title: Avoid a second post-run rejection cleanup for failures already cleaned by train_model.
low_recommendations.observation: On a training-step end failure, train_model invokes on_train_cleanup(False), then train_process invokes the same hook again in its catch. The probe excludes the separate initialization cleanup and records two post-run False calls. A combined failure raises the secondary cleanup error again; Python exception context still retains the original end error.
low_recommendations.recommendation: While correcting the acceptance boundary, give rejection cleanup one clear owner per failed stage and preserve useful primary/secondary exception visibility. Built-in SCAFFOLD cleanup is idempotent here; this observation is not an additional demonstrated model/control corruption finding or a demand for transactions across arbitrary composed plugins.

primary_source.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
primary_source.authority: Main Algorithm 1 and equations (3)-(5), PDF pages 4-5; independently re-opened primary PDF. Appendix displacement sign typo is not the implementation authority.
primary_source.equations_checked: y_next=y-eta*(g-ci+c); ci_new=ci-c+(x-y)/(K*eta); c_new=c+sum(delta_ci)/N. Constant vanilla SGD gives ci_new equal to the mean actually used gradients. Shipped unequal-sample model averaging and optimizer extensions remain explicitly bounded implementation choices.

Additional finite control-sum/delta-arithmetic overflow and NaN receive callbacks on either zero-weight client pass. Postcommit reporting failure retains accepted x=8,c=13/3 as intended.

Unmodified shipped SGD momentum=.9/lr=.01 and constant-rate Adam match independent raw optimizer updates followed by subtractive correction; one visible extension warning per run. V2 is the shared corrected Option II subclass. No mean-gradient/convergence equivalence claimed for optimizer extensions.
